title: The upright piano in the parlor and his mother's aims
summary: Basie describes the big upright piano at home and says his mother simply wanted him to learn to play, not to become a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was the piano that you had at home?
Did you have a piano at home?
I think everybody had a piano.
Yeah, where else? In the kitchen?
People do all kinds of things.
But in them days, I think they always had the piano in the parlor.
You can have a piano almost anywhere now, you know.
They make them kind of pianos, too.
Well, they fit everywhere, you know, like the little Spinets, little pianos like that. There's hardly a place for a big upright piano to go (inaudible).
(Inaudible) unless those people have the large dining rooms or something like that.
Well, was it a Spinet? I
Yeah, big piano that somebody would have 60 years ago.
But your mother wanted you to become a musician or just wanted you --
She wanted me to play. I mean, about as far as I mean that -- I don't think the word musician student would come up then. I mean, just wanted you to play piano.
That was the idea of having piano lessons.
I don't think anybody was taking piano lessons to become -- to actually become a musician.
I see. In other words, it's to be able to play the piano at home.

I think they have a certain amount, you know, the scales and things like that. I'm always seeing that happen in school.
